title.narrative: Media Recovery and Research: Strengthening Ukraine’s Independent Journalism for Sustainable Reconstruction

description.narrative: UNESCO, in partnership with Lviv Media Forum, will continue to support recovery of the Ukrainian media sector through research. Building on data from the RDNA4, this initiative will conduct research to regularly update damage, loss, and recovery needs, ensuring an evidence-based approach to media reconstruction. Following the successful development of a methodology for RDNA assessments on media and the first-time comprehensive inclusion of media in RDNA4 in Ukraine, this will further serve to strengthen not only approaches to media recovery in Ukraine, but also further bolster UNESCO’s ability to lead media recovery assessments globally. Based on identified needs, the project will include targeted capacity-building programs for local and regional independent media, helping them continue during ongoing war and adapt to the post-war landscape through financial sustainability training, journalism education, and strategies for audience engagement. Additionally, it will facilitate knowledge-sharing between Ukrainian and international media experts to strengthen the sector’s role in promoting transparency in the recovery process. By combining research with capacity-building support, this project will provide both immediate assistance and long-term strategies to rebuild a strong, viable, and independent media environment in Ukraine.
